profile.headline: Entrepreneur / Innovator in Biotech and Finance
profile.summary:
Eric Blackstone is a multifaceted entrepreneur and innovator in biotech and finance. In December 2023, he co-founded Bitcoin is For Everyone, a nonprofit aiming to democratize financial technology and advocate for the inclusive use of Bitcoin as a currency. To strengthen his programming skills, he undertook a software development internship in 2022.

For several years Eric worked as a freelance technical copywriter, where he utilized his extensive knowledge in medical writing and pharmaceutical advertising to craft compelling content.

Earlier in his career, Eric served as a Technology Manager at the University of Washington Center for Commercialization, where he played a pivotal role in technology transfer and commercialization efforts. This experience ignited Eric's entrepreneurial spirit, leading him to co-found Nova TheraNostics LLC, a biotech company that emerged from the University of Washington.

Eric's academic journey is as diverse as his professional one. He earned a BS in Biology from the University of Rochester; in addition, he pursued a PhD in Molecular Biology at the University of Washington while simultaneously earning an MBA in the evenings. His groundbreaking doctoral research introduced an innovative approach to induce artificial hibernation in mammals, laying the foundation for the biopharmaceutical company, Ikaria.

positions.title: Technical Copywriter
positions.description: Remote, project-based, freelance technical copywriter with experience in medical writing and pharmaceutical advertising, focused on rare diseases and hematology/oncology. Open to working in other biotech/pharmaceutical/medical fields.

positions.title: Group Copy Supervisor
positions.description: As part of the advertising team, I focused on creating/editing/fact-checking educational and promotional materials concerning drugs useful for treating conditions in hematology/oncology. The main target of the materials were healthcare professionals (HCPs), and I occasionally contributed to materials that were more patient focused.

positions.title: Technical Copywriter
positions.description: For my first foray into pharmaceutical advertising, I helped the team create training materials concerning drugs useful for treating very rare diseases. These materials were targeted to health care professionals in many settings including conferences, journal articles, and training sessions. My main contributions were in fact-checking, editing, and technical copywriting for these pieces.

positions.title: Commercialization Postdoctoral Fellow
positions.description:
•	Optimized lab techniques for large-scale production of lipid nanoparticles in a GMP facility
•	Awarded several commercialization grants totaling over $400,000 
•	Presented to the Innovation Showcase, New Ventures Advisory Board, X/Seed Capital,  WINGS, and other local investment groups
•	Identified a regulatory specialist and have been working with her extensively to create a regulatory plan, including a pre-IND meeting
•	Identified lab space to occupy once we receive funding
•	Vetted CROs for both the manufacture of our agent under GMP standards and for pre-clinical toxicology tests under GLP standards
•	Identified potential centers for a Phase I FDA clinical trial
•	Contacted many VC, Angel, and potential Industry partners for future funding
•	Identified and hired experienced biotech CEO to focus on raising Series A

positions.title: Technology Manager
positions.description:
•	Executed over 50 licenses to transfer technology from the University to industry
•	Drafted and oversaw inter-institutional agreements for co-owned inventions
•	Negotiated with entrepreneurs and university scientists to create startup companies
•	Consulted with both internal and external attorneys to manage university IP and contracts
•	Maintained all responsibilities as Licensing Associate (see below)

positions.title: Licensing Associate
positions.description:
• Evaluate new technologies for commercialization
     — Analyze patentability prospects and identify prior art
     — Research markets and contact potential licensees
• Manage the Biological Materials Portfolio
     — Market the portfolio actively to relevant companies
     — Draft and negotiate term sheets and licenses
• Develop online resources describing technologies available for licensing

patents.title: USE OF CHALCOGENIDES FOR TREATING SHOCK AND OTHER ADVERSE CONDITIONS
patents.description: The present invention concerns the use of active compounds for inducing apnea and treating shock, in addition to enhancing the survivability of a subject. It includes compositions, methods, articles of manufacture and apparatuses for enhancing survivability and for achieving these effects.

patents.title: METHODS, COMPOSITIONS AND ARTICLES OF MANUFACTURE FOR ENHANCING SURVIVABILITY OF CELLS, TISSUES, ORGANS, AND ORGANISMS
patents.description: The present invention concerns the use of oxygen antagonists and other active compounds for inducing stasis or pre-stasis in cells, tissues, and/or organs in vivo or in an organism overall, in addition to enhancing their survivability. It includes compositions, methods, articles of manufacture and apparatuses for enhancing survivability and for achieving stasis or pre-stasis in any of these biological materials, so as to preserve and/or protect them. In specific embodiments, there are also therapeutic methods and apparatuses for organ transplantation, hyperthermia, wound healing, hemorrhagic shock, cardioplegia for bypass surgery, neurodegeneration, hypothermia, and cancer using the active compounds described.
